audit_member_text: Real and integer MGPU periodic paths repeatedly call `cudaMemcpy2D` with pitches and widths expressed as Mloc or Mloc-2*Nghost (for example L1001-L1011 and the analogous integer block). The file does not state whether the CUDA Fortran overload interprets these quantities as elements or bytes; if it follows the byte-count API, REAL(SP)/INTEGER rows are under-copied by their element size. The interface definition is outside this file and must be checked.

The real PY==1 periodic copies omit an explicit cudaMemcpy kind while the analogous integer copies include cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice. Whether overload inference makes the two paths equivalent is not documented here.

Boundary kernels iterate through expanded Ibeg-1:Iend+1/Jbeg-1:Jend+1 ranges and write neighboring indices such as I+1 or J+1. Safety assumes at least the corresponding ghost width and consistent Iend/Jend placement; the kernels receive no Mloc/Nloc and perform no outer allocation-bound check.

VTYPE 4 y-boundary handling is explicitly described as not an exact solution and simply zeros cross-derivative ghosts (around L1320-L1417); the approximation's effect and intended conditions are not specified.

The generic interface declares module procedures with the same generic/specific spelling `PHI_COLL_GPU` plus `PHI_COLL_INT_GPU` at L38-L41. Compiler acceptance of a generic sharing the real specific's name is compiler-language-version dependent and is not established here.
